newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 17.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Tuesday.

- Sinn Fein leader Gerry Adams, in the face of persistent speculation, has emphatically denied any knowledge of Irish Republican Army (IRA) plans to hold an "army convention" meeting leading to a renewed ceasefire.
- Direct Action Against Drugs, viewed as a cover name for the IRA, has admitted the murder of Sean Devlin in the Markets area of Belfast on Thursday.
- The pilots dispute at Irish airline Aer Lingus escalated on Monday when the company warned that unless negotiations opened immediately it would be forced to issue protective notice to staff.
- Two Irish students, a man aged 26 and a woman aged 27, have died in a fire in New York State.
- A top level report has shown that Ireland's Social Welfare Department under minister Prionsias De Rossa grossly underestimated the extent of social welfare fraud.
- A new report on the Dublin light rail scheme clashes on a number of fundamental points with an earlier survey prepared for the project team by design consultants.
- John Cunningham, one of two brothers who kidnapped banker's wife Jennifer Guinness, escaped from prison on Monday after he walked out of an open jail in County Wicklow.
